learning_outcomes.text: Plans, executes, and interprets machine tests.
Applies experimental techniques to mechanical systems.
Designs experimental systems for machine testing.

Analyzes a problem and designs an algorithm to solve it. Understands and applies different algorithmic control structures. Works with files capable of storing large amounts of data. Represents data graphically and manipulates it effectively. Designs processes for the numerical solution of problems with linear and non-linear equation systems.
Determines loads on machine elements using experimental methods.

Plans communication: generates ideas, searches for information, selects and orders information, creates outlines, determines the audience type, communication objectives,... Drafts documents with appropriate format, content, structure, linguistic correctness, register, and illustrates concepts correctly using conventions: formats, titles, footers, legends,...

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Makes individual contributions within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group rules. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

Collects significant information needed to solve problems based on objective criteria. Follows a logical method to identify the causes of a problem. Presents different alternative solution options for the same problem and evaluates their possible risks and advantages. Develops a strategy to solve the problem. Obtains necessary support from others to achieve the success of their decisions. Has the ability to lead the decision-making process participatively. Methodically questions new ways of doing things, seeks new procedures, and experiments with new procedures. Analyzes risks and benefits of innovation.

syllabus_topics: Presentation
Signal analysis in the time domain
Introduction to MATLAB for signal analysis
Signal processing in the time domain with MATLAB
Introduction to signal analysis in the frequency domain
Introduction to MATLAB for signal analysis
Signal processing in the frequency domain with MATLAB
Sensors, data acquisition systems, and experimental system characterization
Flexible data acquisition system
Sensor calibration
Obtaining the uncertainty associated with the sensor (hysteresis, linearity, etc.)
Signal sampling and reconstruction
Image-based experimental system
Study of sampling and reconstruction using numerical simulation
Free vibrations of 1 GDL systems
Theoretical study (reduced model) of a tuning fork
Experimental study (audio signal analysis) of the tuning fork
Shake table
Theoretical study (reduced model) of a series of rods with different configurations
Experimental study (shake table) of a series of rods with different configurations
Forced vibrations of 1 GDL systems
Theoretical analysis (reduced model) of forced vibrations in a washing machine
Experimental analysis of forced vibrations in a washing machine using accelerometers
Study of damping effects
Equivalence of dry (Coulomb) and viscous damping
Vibrations of N GDL and continuous systems
Theoretical study (2 GDL reduced model) of a two-story building model
Experimental study (shake table) of the two-story building model
Theoretical study (one-dimensional standing wave model) of a vibrating string
Experimental study (stroboscopic illumination, exciter, etc.) of a vibrating string
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Presentation of the syllabus, methodology to follow, evaluation, and work required to successfully complete the course.
Lectures: Explanation of topics and theoretical concepts associated with laboratory practices.
Laboratory practices: Carrying out laboratory practices either on computers or with experimental setups prepared by the professors.
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the minimum grade in any test/exam must be greater than or equal to 3.5 points. Attendance to theory and practical sessions is mandatory; only one unjustified absence from practices is allowed. Failure to recover any practice within the established period implies failing the course. For the second call, there will be an exam including practical tests and/or multiple-choice tests, covering all course material, with a weight of 100%.
